text.p: A group holding 5.2 percent of Universal Seismic Associates Inc stock said on Wednesday it was dissatisified with recent management actions, and was considering calling a meeting to remove company directors.
In particular, the group said it was concerned by the expiry of a merger letter of intent between Universal Seismic and Suelopetrol c.a. of Venezuela.

""We've been working on this transaction since May 1996 and to have come this far, without completing the process, would be totally unacceptable," said Michael Kanarellis, who formed the group with Robert Kecseg.
The letter of intent, dated August 1, 1996, was the responsibility of the board of directors and company management, the group said.
"If this transaction creates shareholder value, it should be concluded," said Kanarellis, president of TechnoFlex.

Although Universal Seismic said it was continuing to discuss terms with Suelopetrol, the group said it believed the expiration of the letter of intent and the company's apparent failure to complete an intensive review of the situation had jeopardized the merger's completion.
Universal Seismic, which provides three-dimensional seismic mapping and data processing services to the energy industry, was not immediately available for comment.

The members of the group said they filed Schedule 13Ds on Tuesday with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission indicating that the group beneficially owned a combined 5.2 stake on the shares outstanding.
Potential responses included compelling the board of directors to call a shareholder meeting to remove at least a majority of the company's directors, the group said.
